title: Atoms, isotopes and a dilution
promptMarkdown:
Three short checks on atoms, isotopes and solutions.

1. For the ion $\ce{^{37}_{17}Cl^-}$ state the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons.
2. Chlorine has two stable isotopes: $\ce{^{35}Cl}$ (mass 34.969 u, abundance 75.76%) and $\ce{^{37}Cl}$ (mass 36.966 u, abundance 24.24%). Compute the average atomic mass and explain in one sentence why no single chlorine atom has this mass.
3. $5.85\ \text{g}$ of $\ce{NaCl}$ ($M = 58.44\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$) is dissolved in water and made up to $250.0\ \text{mL}$ of solution. Compute the molarity. Then $50.0\ \text{mL}$ of this solution is diluted to $200.0\ \text{mL}$: compute the new molarity of $\ce{NaCl}$ and the concentration of chloride ions in the diluted solution. State the assumption about volumes that a dilution calculation makes.
hintLadder: In $\ce{^{A}_{Z}X^{q}}$ the lower-left number is the proton count, the upper-left number counts protons plus neutrons, and the charge tells you how many electrons were gained or lost.
An average atomic mass is an abundance-weighted mean: multiply each isotopic mass by its fractional abundance and add.
Molarity is moles of solute per litre of final solution; convert millilitres to litres.
Dilution conserves the amount of solute: $c_1V_1 = c_2V_2$. Then ask how many chloride ions each formula unit of $\ce{NaCl}$ supplies.

checkExamples.label: correct answer
checkExamples.text: 17 protons, 20 neutrons (37 − 17), 18 electrons (17 + 1 for the negative charge). Average mass = 0.7576(34.969) + 0.2424(36.966) = 35.45 u; it is a weighted mean over the two isotopes, so no atom has it. n = 5.85/58.44 = 0.1001 mol; c = 0.1001/0.2500 = 0.400 M. Diluted: 0.400 × 50.0/200.0 = 0.100 M NaCl, and [Cl−] = 0.100 M since each formula unit gives one chloride. The dilution assumes the amount of solute is conserved and the final solution volume is the 200.0 mL stated.
